programmes.funder: Biotechnology and Biological Sciences Research Council (UKRI)
programmes.amount_note: Commercialisation funding to translate BBSRC-remit research towards market; typical awards up to around GBP 250,000, with a 'Pathfinder' strand for smaller early awards.
programmes.deadline_note: Historically ran with two to three cut-offs a year.

eligibility.other_note: Applicant must be eligible for UKRI funding (university or research institute); spinouts benefit indirectly.

programmes.name_en: Big Issue Invest social enterprise investment
programmes.amount_note: Social investment through loans and equity to social enterprises and mission-led businesses. Ticket sizes range from tens of thousands of pounds for early-stage lending to several million for growth capital.
programmes.deadline_note: Applications assessed on a rolling basis; specific funds (for example the Impact Loans England programme) may have their own windows.

eligibility.other_note: UK social enterprises, charities and mission-locked businesses that can demonstrate social impact and repayment capacity.

programmes.amount_note: Strategic venture investment in energy transition companies. Cheque sizes are not published.

programmes.name_local: Business Wales start-up support and Big Ideas Wales
programmes.name_en: Business Wales start-up support and Big Ideas Wales
programmes.amount_note: Free adviser support, start-up workshops, mentoring and the Big Ideas Wales programme for young entrepreneurs (18-25). Not a cash grant.

eligibility.other_note: Big Ideas Wales includes a Bootcamp and the Big Ideas Wales Challenge for 18-25 year olds.

programmes.funder: Cambridge Enterprise Ltd, University of Cambridge
programmes.amount_note: GIVEN: seed and pre-seed equity investment into University of Cambridge spin-outs and student/alumni startups, usually alongside external co-investors. TAKEN: an equity stake, plus (for spin-outs licensing university IP) a separate founding stake under the university's spin-out policy. Ticket sizes are negotiated per deal and not published as a standard figure.
programmes.deadline_note: Rolling. Cambridge Enterprise assesses opportunities continuously, with investment committees held regularly.

eligibility.other_note: Company must have a University of Cambridge connection, typically as a spin-out based on university IP or a startup founded by Cambridge students, staff or recent alumni.

programmes.funder: Cancer Research UK / Cancer Research Horizons
programmes.amount_note: Multiple routes including Biotherapeutics Development, Early Detection and Diagnosis Innovation Awards and translational/seed investment. Amounts vary substantially by route.
programmes.deadline_note: Individual schemes have their own deadlines; the Early Detection and Diagnosis Innovation Award has historically had annual or biannual cut-offs.

eligibility.other_note: Cancer Research Horizons is CRUK's innovation arm; it both grant-funds and takes equity in spinouts.

programmes.name_local: Cancer Research UK Therapeutic Discovery Laboratories partnerships
programmes.name_en: Cancer Research UK Therapeutic Discovery Laboratories co-development
programmes.funder: Cancer Research UK (via Cancer Research Horizons)
programmes.amount_note: CRUK co-develops oncology therapeutics with academic groups and biotechs, funding preclinical and clinical work in exchange for a share of future returns rather than paying a cash grant to the company.
programmes.deadline_note: Partnership opportunities are assessed on a rolling basis through Cancer Research Horizons.

eligibility.other_note: Focus on oncology; UK-based academic groups and companies are the main route, but international partnerships are considered.

programmes.name_en: Carbon13 (The Venture Builder for the Climate Emergency)
programmes.amount_note: GIVEN: a paid founder position during the venture-building programme (a living allowance while you form a team and validate an idea) plus an investment into the companies formed at the end. TAKEN: an equity stake in the new company. Carbon13 runs cohorts in Cambridge/London and Berlin; confirm the current allowance and investment terms in the live cohort documentation.
programmes.deadline_note: Cohort-based with periodic application deadlines, typically two to three cohorts per year across its UK and German programmes.

eligibility.other_note: Applications are from individuals (founders, scientists, commercial operators), not from formed companies. The target is ventures capable of abating 10 million tonnes of CO2e per year.

programmes.name_local: Carbon13 Venture Builder for the Climate Emergency (Cambridge)
programmes.amount_note: Eight-month venture builder for a cohort of around 80 individuals. Carbon13 has historically invested a pre-seed cheque in the ventures formed during the programme in exchange for equity; current terms are not published on the homepage.
programmes.deadline_note: Cohorts recruited via 'Apply Now' rounds; specific deadlines are published on the application portal rather than the homepage.

eligibility.other_note: For individuals from the UK and beyond who do not yet have a startup but want to find a co-founder and build a climate-tech company. Average cohort age 37; a third hold PhDs.

programmes.source_snippet: An eight-month programme for a cohort of 80 determined individuals from the UK and beyond, who don't have a startup yet but want to find a co-founder and build a climate-tech startup.

programmes.amount_note: GIVES NO STANDARD CASH CHEQUE and takes no equity for the core programme: a part-time venture programme that trains PhD students to turn their research into a company while still doing the PhD. programmes.deadline_note: Annual cohort aligned to the UK academic year; applications typically close in the summer for an autumn start.
programmes.reopen_note: Conception X has recruited an annual cohort each year since 2018; applications reopen in spring for the autumn programme.

eligibility.other_note: For PhD students and postdocs at UK universities. No company or prior commercial experience required.

programmes.name_local: Cornwall and Isles of Scilly business grants (Good Growth / Shared Prosperity Fund)
programmes.name_en: Cornwall and Isles of Scilly business grants (Good Growth / Shared Prosperity Fund)
programmes.funder: Cornwall Council / Cornwall and Isles of Scilly Growth Hub
programmes.amount_note: Cornwall receives a distinct Good Growth settlement. Grant schemes have included capital investment, net zero, digital and innovation grants; many cap in the GBP 1,000-50,000 range at 30-50% intervention, with larger capital grants for significant projects.
programmes.deadline_note: Individual grant calls open and close as budget allows; several run each year.

eligibility.other_note: Cornwall retained a bespoke funding settlement after EU structural funds ended. Also home to Spaceport Cornwall and a strong marine/floating offshore wind cluster.

programmes.funder: Defence and Security Accelerator (DASA), Ministry of Defence
programmes.amount_note: Phase 1 proposals typically up to around GBP 350,000 (Rapid Impact awards commonly up to ~GBP 100,000 over 6 months; Fast Track/Phase 2 awards larger). 100% funded R&D contracts, supplier retains background IP.
programmes.deadline_note: Historically ran as continuous calendar-year cycles with cut-offs roughly every 6-8 weeks (for example CY2025 Cycle 4). Two routes: Rapid Impact and Rapid Impact - Emerging Innovations.
programmes.reopen_note: MOD launched UK Defence Innovation (UKDI) in July 2025 with a GBP 400m budget, consolidating defence innovation activity including DASA. Check GOV.UK's DASA/UKDI collection pages for the current cycle - branding and process are in transition.

Optionally book a DASA innovation partner conversation
Submit through the DASA online submission service before the cycle cut-off
Assessment against desirability, feasibility and viability
Contract award as a funded R&D contract

Company details and financial viability information

eligibility.other_note: Funded via R&D contracts rather than grants, so VAT and contract terms apply. Open to companies, academics and individuals; overseas suppliers can apply but must meet security requirements.

eligibility.other_note: Themes are set by MOD and Home Office customers; read each competition document for scope.

programmes.name_en: Development Bank of Wales Flexible Investment Fund

eligibility.other_note: For established Welsh businesses; requires demonstrable repayment capacity.

programmes.name_local: Development Bank of Wales Micro Loan Fund
programmes.name_en: Development Bank of Wales Micro Loan Fund
programmes.amount_note: Loans from GBP 1,000 to GBP 50,000 for start-ups and micro businesses in Wales, over terms up to around 10 years.

eligibility.other_note: Business must be based in Wales or relocating to Wales. Wales-specific alternative to Start Up Loans, and can be combined with it in some cases.

eligibility.other_note: Company must be based in Wales. The Development Bank also runs an angel co-investment fund and manages Angels Invest Wales.

TAKEN: a founding equity stake in the new company - DSV is a co-founder, not a passive investor, so its stake is materially larger than a typical accelerator's. Exact salary and equity split are set per programme and sector.
programmes.deadline_note: Recruits Founders-in-Residence in sector cohorts (climate, computation, pharma, agriculture) with periodic application deadlines.

eligibility.other_note: For individual scientists and technologists, typically post-PhD, willing to start a new company from a DSV-defined problem area rather than bring their own existing venture.

programmes.funder: Department for Energy Security and Net Zero (DESNZ)
programmes.amount_note: Historically grants of roughly GBP 100,000 to GBP 1 million plus incubation support for SMEs developing energy efficiency, power generation, heat and storage technologies.
programmes.deadline_note: Ran in numbered phases (Phases 1-9) roughly annually since 2012, each with a several-week application window.
programmes.reopen_note: No confirmed new phase announced as at August 2026. The EEF has historically returned in new phases under successive energy departments; watch GOV.UK and the DESNZ innovation funding pages. Similar SME support now flows through Net Zero Innovation Portfolio competitions.

eligibility.other_note: Targeted at SMEs; grants historically required significant match funding.

programmes.funder: Department for Energy Security and Net Zero (DESNZ)
programmes.amount_note: Umbrella portfolio funding hydrogen, long-duration energy storage, heat pumps, industrial fuel switching, CCUS, floating offshore wind and more. Individual competition awards range from tens of thousands to tens of millions.
programmes.deadline_note: Delivered as a series of separate themed competitions, each with its own window.

eligibility.other_note: Check the GOV.UK NZIP collection page for which sub-competitions are currently live.

programmes.funder: Department for Transport / Connected Places Catapult
programmes.amount_note: Small early-stage feasibility grants, historically around GBP 30,000-45,000 per project, 100% funded, plus commercialisation support from Connected Places Catapult.
programmes.deadline_note: Annual competition, historically opening in the spring or summer with a 4-6 week window.
programmes.reopen_note: TRIG has run annually since 2014 with several themed strands each year. Watch the Connected Places Catapult and DfT pages, typically from around April to July.

eligibility.other_note: Very early stage - one of the most accessible UK transport innovation entry points. Individuals and academics can often apply as well as companies.

programmes.name_local: CyberASAP (Cyber Security Academic Startup Accelerator Programme)
programmes.name_en: CyberASAP (Cyber Security Academic Startup Accelerator Programme)
programmes.funder: Department for Science, Innovation and Technology / Innovate UK Business Connect
programmes.amount_note: Phased funding across value proposition, proof of concept and demonstrator phases; total funding across phases has historically been up to around GBP 90,000 per team, paid to the university.
programmes.deadline_note: Annual cohort, historically opening in the spring/summer with the programme running across the academic year.
programmes.reopen_note: CyberASAP has run annually since 2017. Watch the Innovate UK Business Connect CyberASAP pages, usually from around April to July for the next cohort.

eligibility.other_note: Only UK academics with cyber security research can apply; the aim is to form a spinout.

programmes.reopen_note: Runs annually. To be considered you must be nominated by one of the accredited Nominator organisations; the nomination window usually opens around the turn of the year.

eligibility.other_note: Open to companies, nonprofits, communities and governments worldwide across five Earthshots

programmes.name_en: ESA Business Incubation Centre United Kingdom

programmes.deadline_note: This ESA BIC runs its own call cycle with published cut-off dates, typically two to four per year. Contact the local centre for the next deadline.

Submit application documents before the local deadline
Tender Opening Board review, then presentation to the Tender Evaluation Board
Register a company in United Kingdom before signing the incubation contract

TAKEN: an equity stake, typically high single digits, reflecting both the cash and the services. Amounts differ by programme and corporate partner; the venture studio (Founders Factory builds companies from scratch) takes a substantially larger founding stake than the accelerator. Confirm the split of cash versus services before signing.
programmes.deadline_note: Rolling intake into corporate-partnered accelerator tracks; programmes also operate in Africa (Founders Factory Africa) and other regions with their own terms.

eligibility.other_note: Sector fit is driven by which corporate partners are funding the track at the time (media, retail, health, energy, fintech have all featured).

programmes.amount_note: Debt and equity into London SMEs, commonly GBP 100,000-1 million for debt and larger for equity, delivered by appointed fund managers.

eligibility.other_note: Apply to the appointed fund managers, not to Funding London directly.

programmes.name_local: Grow London / London and Partners business growth support
programmes.name_en: Grow London / London and Partners business growth support
programmes.funder: Greater London Authority / London and Partners
programmes.amount_note: Free scaleup support, international expansion programmes (Grow London Global), investor introductions and soft-landing support. Not usually a cash grant.
programmes.deadline_note: Grow London Global and similar cohort programmes recruit periodically.

eligibility.other_note: London and Partners is the Mayor's growth agency. Grow London Global is a competitive cohort programme for scaleups expanding overseas.

programmes.name_local: GC Business Growth Hub - grants and business support
programmes.name_en: GC Business Growth Hub - grants and business support
programmes.funder: Greater Manchester Combined Authority / The Growth Company
programmes.amount_note: Runs a changing portfolio of funded programmes - digital adoption, net zero, productivity and innovation grants. Individual grants have commonly been GBP 1,000-25,000 at around 40-50% intervention, with larger capital grants in some strands.
programmes.deadline_note: Individual grant schemes open and close as budgets allow; the Growth Hub itself operates continuously.

procedure_steps.detail: Register with GC Business Growth Hub
Diagnostic call with a business adviser
Adviser matches you to an open grant or support programme
Apply to the specific scheme

eligibility.other_note: Business must be based in one of the ten Greater Manchester boroughs. Check which specific grant programmes are live - they are budget-limited and turn over frequently.

programmes.name_local: Highlands and Islands Enterprise business and innovation support
programmes.name_en: Highlands and Islands Enterprise business and innovation support
programmes.amount_note: Discretionary account-managed support covering innovation, capital investment, skills and international trade. Amounts negotiated per project against subsidy control limits.
programmes.deadline_note: Rolling; contact your HIE area office.

eligibility.other_note: Covers Argyll and Bute, Highland, Moray, Orkney, Shetland, Western Isles and parts of north Argyll. HIE also runs Northern Innovation Hub and rural-specific programmes.

programmes.amount_note: Up to GBP 5 million a year and GBP 12 million lifetime (GBP 10 million a year / GBP 20 million lifetime for knowledge-intensive companies). Investors receive 30% income tax relief.
programmes.deadline_note: Continuous. Advance assurance recommended before the raise.

procedure_steps.detail: Confirm the company meets the age, size and trade conditions
Apply to HMRC for advance assurance
Issue the shares
Submit form EIS1 compliance statement
HMRC issues EIS3 certificates

eligibility.other_note: Generally under 7 years from first commercial sale (10 for knowledge-intensive), fewer than 250 employees (500 for KIC) and gross assets under GBP 15 million before investment.

programmes.name_local: R&D tax relief (merged RDEC scheme and Enhanced R&D Intensive Support)
programmes.name_en: R&D tax relief (merged RDEC scheme and Enhanced R&D Intensive Support)

Prepare the Additional Information Form detailing projects and costs
Include the claim in the CT600 Corporation Tax return

eligibility.other_note: The most widely used non-dilutive funding in the UK for R&D startups. Note grant funding can affect subsidy treatment - take advice if you also hold an Innovate UK grant.

Request advance assurance from HMRC
Issue shares to investors

HMRC issues SEIS3 certificates for investors

eligibility.other_note: Business must be based in Northern Ireland. The knowledge provider must be on Invest NI's approved list.

programmes.amount_note: Pre-accelerator for early-stage founders, historically including a living allowance of around GBP 15,000-25,000 over the programme plus training and mentoring.
programmes.deadline_note: Annual or biannual cohort intake.

programmes.amount_note: Reduced Corporation Tax rate of 10% on profits earned from patented inventions. Value depends entirely on the company's qualifying IP income and the R&D fraction; there is no cap.
programmes.deadline_note: Election must be made within 2 years after the end of the accounting period in which the relevant profits and income arose.

procedure_steps.detail: Confirm the company owns or exclusively licences-in qualifying patents (UK IPO, EPO or listed EEA offices) and has undertaken qualifying development.
Separate relevant IP income from other income (streaming) and work through the Patent Box calculation steps.
Elect into the Patent Box in the computations accompanying the Company Tax Return, or separately in writing.

documents_required.doc: Written election into the Patent Box (or election in the CT computations)
documents_required.note: No special form of words and no box on the CT return

documents_required.doc: Patent Box calculation showing relevant IP profits

eligibility.other_note: Company must be liable to Corporation Tax and make a profit from exploiting patented inventions. Certain medicinal or botanic innovation rights also qualify. Benefits restricted by the R&D fraction where patents were acquired or R&D was paid to connected parties (for elections after 30 June 2016).

programmes.source_snippet: Companies must elect into the Patent Box to apply the lower rate of Corporation Tax which is 10%.

programmes.name_en: R&D expenditure credit (RDEC) for accounting periods beginning before 1 April 2024
programmes.amount_note: Credit of 20% of qualifying costs incurred 1 April 2023 to 31 March 2024 (13% for 1 April 2020 to 31 March 2023). Only relevant now for late or amended claims covering accounting periods that began before 1 April 2024; superseded by the merged RDEC scheme.
programmes.deadline_note: Applies only to accounting periods beginning before 1 April 2024. New periods must use the merged RDEC scheme or ERIS. Included because amended/late claims for earlier periods are still possible.

procedure_steps.detail: Confirm the accounting period began before 1 April 2024 and you fall in an eligible category (large company, or SME claiming subcontracted, state-aided or otherwise subsidised work).
Claim through the Company Tax Return with the additional information form.

documents_required.doc: Company Tax Return (CT600) with R&D claim

eligibility.other_note: SMEs used this scheme where work was subcontracted to them, where they received notified State Aid, or where costs were subsidised (e.g. by a grant).

programmes.source_snippet: The tax credit is worked out as a percentage of your qualifying R&D costs. The rate on costs from: ... 1 April 2023 up to and including 31 March 2024 is 20%

programmes.name_local: Scottish Enterprise Research and Development (R&D) grants
programmes.name_en: Scottish Enterprise Research and Development (R&D) grants
programmes.amount_note: The minimum grant considered is £250,000. SMEs working independently may receive a grant covering between 35% and 50% of eligible project costs; large companies working independently between 25% and 40%. Consortiums of 2-6 companies may receive slightly higher rates in certain circumstances. Projects should represent at least £1 million of company spend.
programmes.deadline_note: No fixed deadline; enquiries assessed on an ongoing basis.

procedure_steps.detail: Download and complete the enquiry form.
Send the completed form to enquiries@scotent.co.uk.
Receive feedback and, if appropriate, meet an appraisal specialist.
Progress through the formal application process.

eligibility.other_note: Business must be based in, or planning to locate in, Scotland in the area served by Scottish Enterprise. Project must represent a significant innovation for the company and could not proceed (or would be significantly delayed or reduced) without the funding. Sole traders and charities are ineligible, as are companies relying primarily on third parties for the R&D or that have already started work. Note: the separate SMART: SCOTLAND grant scheme is currently on hold.

programmes.source_snippet: Small or medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) working independently on innovative projects may receive a grant to cover between 35% and 50% of their eligible project costs. ... The minimum grant considered is £250,000.

programmes.amount_note: A company can receive a maximum of £250,000 through SEIS over its lifetime. NOTE: SEIS is an INVESTOR tax relief, not money paid to the company — HMRC gives income tax and CGT reliefs to individuals who subscribe for shares. It is recorded here as a tax_credit because SEIS status is in practice a precondition for most UK pre-seed rounds and materially improves a startup's ability to raise; the £250,000 is the cap on qualifying investment the company may take in, not a grant.
programmes.deadline_note: No deadline; advance assurance can be requested at any time, and the compliance statement is filed after shares are issued.

procedure_steps.detail: Optionally apply to HMRC for advance assurance that the proposed share issue will qualify.
Issue the shares to investors.
Once you have carried out the qualifying trade for at least 4 months or spent at least 70% of the money raised, submit compliance statement form SEIS1 to HMRC.
HMRC issues compliance certificates (SEIS3) for you to pass to investors.

documents_required.note: Needed for an advance assurance request

eligibility.other_note: If already carrying out a qualifying trade, it must not have been carried out for more than 3 years. Gross assets must not exceed £350,000 when the shares are issued, and the company must have fewer than 25 full-time equivalent employees. Certain trades are excluded.

programmes.source_snippet: You can receive a maximum of £250,000 through Seed Enterprise Investment Scheme.

programmes.name_en: British Business Bank Start Up Loans
programmes.funder: The Start Up Loans Company (British Business Bank)
programmes.amount_note: Unsecured personal loan of up to £25,000 (average loan £10,264) at a fixed interest rate of 7.5% per year, repayable over 1-5 years. No fees for arranging the loan or for early repayment. Includes 12 months of free business mentoring for first-time recipients.
programmes.deadline_note: Applications accepted at any time.

procedure_steps.detail: Check eligibility criteria (UK resident, business trading less than 60 months, credit check).
Register and apply online.
Work with a delivery partner to complete a business plan and cash flow forecast.
If approved, receive funds and 12 months of free mentoring.

documents_required.note: It is a personal loan, so personal finances are assessed

eligibility.other_note: Available to people starting a new business or trading for less than 60 months. It is an unsecured personal loan to the individual, not a company loan, so sole traders and partnerships qualify as well as limited companies.

programmes.source_snippet: Borrow up to £25,000 - Unsecured personal loan - Fixed interest rate of 7.5% per year - Repay the loan over a term of 1-5 years - 12 months of free mentoring - Government-backed
